{{Short description|Any sheaf whose value is based on an eigenfunction}}
{{Context|date=September 2024}}{{One source|date=July 2024}}
In mathematics, a '''Hecke eigensheaf''' is any [[Sheaf (mathematics)|sheaf]] whose [[value (mathematics)|value]] is based on an [[eigenfunction]]. It is an object that is a tensor-multiple of itself when formed under the integral transform of a [[Hecke correspondence]]. Hecke eigensheaves are part of the geometric [[Langlands correspondence]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://people.mpim-bonn.mpg.de/gaitsgde/GLC/Loc.pdf |title= Proof of the geometric Langlands conjecture|date=July 19, 2024 |publisher=Max Planck Institute for Mathematics}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://math.uchicago.edu/~drinfeld/langlands/QuantizationHitchin.pdf&ved=2ahUKEwjVmZTMqbmHAxXihIkEHYoFBSYQFnoECCIQAQ&usg=AOvVaw25SozJZRH1OXDFTDKC9pRy |title= QUANTIZATION OF HITCHIN'S INTEGRABLE SYSTEM AND HECKE|date=1991 |publisher=University of Chicago}}</ref>
